recommendations.regimenLabel: Supportive care + tumour-lysis prophylaxis (definitive chemo by subtype)
steps: Supportive: transfuse as needed, neutropenic-sepsis protocol for fever, tumour-lysis prophylaxis (hydration, allopurinol/rasburicase).
Treat coagulopathy/DIC (esp. APML — start ATRA promptly on suspicion).
Definitive remission-induction chemotherapy per subtype; consider transplant.
Central access, fertility/consent discussions as appropriate.

drugRefs.why: Cornerstone of tumour-lysis-syndrome prophylaxis — maintains high urine flow to clear urate/phosphate before and during cytoreduction.
Prevents new urate formation in standard-risk patients; reduce dose in renal impairment. Does not lower pre-existing urate.
Rapidly degrades existing urate in high tumour-burden disease or established hyperuricaemia. Contraindicated in G6PD deficiency.

drugRefs.regimenLabel: ATRA — start empirically on suspected APML
drugRefs.why: Start promptly on suspicion of acute promyelocytic leukaemia (APML) to correct the coagulopathy/DIC and induce differentiation — do not wait for genetic confirmation.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Acute Myeloid & Lymphoblastic Leukaemia
British Society for Haematology — Management of Tumour Lysis Syndrome

decision.label: Urgent haematology + TLS prophylaxis; ATRA if APML

confirm: Pancytopenia or leucocytosis with blasts on film, bleeding/infection; bone marrow confirms. Watch for tumour lysis/DIC.
